definition: Docile means easily taught, led, or managed — a word for people and animals, not for things.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word docile. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know docile should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The visiting teacher braced for a rowdy afternoon, but the class proved so docile that even the fire drill ran in a straight, silent line.
Agreeable is milder than docile — an agreeable person is simply pleasant company and still pushes back when something matters, while docile means the teaching and leading go through unopposed.
Meek goes further than docile — the docile student still needs a teacher to follow, while the meek one no longer speaks up for itself at all.

Tame means no longer wild — an animal word for creatures at ease around people, however that ease arrived. Docile adds the teaching: docile means easily taught, led, and managed. A stray cat can grow tame with no lessons at all, while a docile horse takes the saddle because teaching goes through smoothly.

Biddable means ready to do as one is bidden, seldom asking why — point, and it goes; ask, and it fetches. Docile is the temperament underneath: a docile animal takes teaching and leading calmly, while biddable describes the moment orders are actually followed.
